questions.prompt: Which group contains only flowering plants?
questions.explanation: Maize and bean plants produce flowers before forming seeds or fruits.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common flowering and non-flowering plants in the local environment.

questions.prompt: A fern is an example of a non-flowering plant.
questions.explanation: Ferns do not produce flowers; they reproduce using tiny spores.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify plants as flowering or non-flowering using observable features.

questions.prompt: Which feature is most useful when deciding that a plant is flowering?
questions.explanation: The presence of flowers is the key feature used to identify flowering plants.
questions.learningOutcome: Use visible plant features to classify common plants.

questions.prompt: Which living thing is a fungus?
questions.explanation: A mushroom is a fungus, not a green plant or an animal.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize common examples of fungi in daily life.

questions.prompt: Yeast is useful in making bread rise.
questions.explanation: Yeast produces gas during fermentation, which helps dough rise.
questions.learningOutcome: State useful roles of fungi in food preparation and the environment.

questions.prompt: Which animal is a vertebrate?
questions.explanation: A chicken has a backbone, so it is a vertebrate.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify animals with backbones as vertebrates.

questions.prompt: Which sense organ helps us hear sounds?
questions.explanation: The ear detects sounds and helps us hear what is around us.
questions.learningOutcome: Name sense organs and state the senses they perform.

questions.prompt: Which part of the body protects the brain?
questions.explanation: The skull is a hard bone structure that protects the brain.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify major bones and describe their protective functions.

questions.prompt: Which organs are mainly used for breathing?
questions.explanation: The lungs help the body take in air and remove waste air during breathing.
questions.learningOutcome: Name main parts of the human breathing system.

questions.prompt: Washing hands with soap can help prevent some worm infections.
questions.explanation: Handwashing removes germs and parasite eggs that may enter the body through food or the mouth.
questions.learningOutcome: State simple hygiene practices that prevent internal parasite infections.

questions.prompt: Which disease is commonly spread through unsafe water?
questions.explanation: Cholera can spread when people drink water contaminated with germs.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of waterborne diseases and how they spread.

questions.prompt: Which item is solid waste?
questions.explanation: A used plastic bottle is solid waste because it is a discarded solid material.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of solid waste found in the local environment.

questions.prompt: Which change happens when ice is heated and becomes water?
questions.explanation: Melting is the change from a solid to a liquid when heat is added.
questions.learningOutcome: Name common changes of state of matter observed in daily life.

questions.prompt: Which software activity is used to type and edit text on a computer?
questions.explanation: Word processing helps users create, edit, format, save, and print text documents.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify word processing as a way to create and edit text documents.

questions.prompt: Which command makes selected text darker and thicker?
questions.explanation: The bold command makes selected text appear darker and thicker.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common formatting commands used in a word processor.

questions.prompt: A learner sees seeds inside a ripe mango. What does this show about the mango plant?
questions.explanation: Fruits with seeds usually form after flowers, so mango is a flowering plant.
questions.learningOutcome: Use fruits and seeds as evidence when classifying flowering plants.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly matches a plant group with an example?
questions.explanation: A fern is a non-flowering plant, while mould is a fungus and maize is a flowering plant.
questions.learningOutcome: Match common organisms to their correct plant or fungus group.

questions.prompt: All mushrooms found in the wild are safe to eat.
questions.explanation: Some wild mushrooms are poisonous, so learners should not eat unknown mushrooms.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe safety precautions when observing or handling fungi.

questions.prompt: Why should mouldy food be avoided?
questions.explanation: Mould can spoil food and may produce substances that make people sick.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe ways of dealing with fungi found on food.

questions.prompt: Which characteristic best describes fish as vertebrates?
questions.explanation: Fish are vertebrates that live in water and breathe mainly using gills.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe observable characteristics of major groups of vertebrates.

questions.prompt: Which group of vertebrates has feathers?
questions.explanation: Feathers are a main body covering of birds.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify vertebrates using body coverings and other features.

questions.prompt: Name one safe way to observe a mushroom during a science activity.
questions.explanation: Using gloves and washing hands after the activity helps learners avoid contact with harmful fungi.
questions.learningOutcome: State safety precautions used when observing fungi.

questions.prompt: Which sense helps a learner know that tea is too hot to drink?
questions.explanation: The skin senses heat, cold, pressure, and pain.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate each sense organ to the information it detects.

questions.prompt: Which practice best protects the eyes?
questions.explanation: Enough light reduces eye strain and helps protect the eyes.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose safe habits for caring for sense organs.

questions.prompt: Which body parts work together to move the arm?
questions.explanation: Muscles pull on bones at joints to produce movement.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how bones, muscles, and joints help the body move.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of the rib cage?
questions.explanation: The rib cage surrounds and protects important organs in the chest.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe protective functions of parts of the skeleton.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct path of air when breathing in?
questions.explanation: Air enters through the nose or mouth, moves through the windpipe, and reaches the lungs.
questions.learningOutcome: Trace the path of air through the breathing system.

questions.prompt: The nose helps filter dust from the air before it reaches the lungs.
questions.explanation: Nose hairs and mucus trap some dust and germs in the air we breathe.
questions.learningOutcome: State functions of parts of the human breathing system.

questions.prompt: Which parasite usually lives outside the body?
questions.explanation: A louse is an external parasite because it lives on the outside of the body.
questions.learningOutcome: Differentiate between external and internal body parasites.

questions.prompt: Which habit can help prevent jigger infestation?
questions.explanation: Wearing shoes protects the feet from jiggers found in dusty or sandy places.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose preventive practices against common external parasites.

questions.prompt: Which action makes drinking water safer at home?
questions.explanation: Boiling water kills many germs that cause waterborne diseases.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify methods of making drinking water safer.

questions.prompt: Using a clean latrine helps reduce the spread of waterborne diseases.
questions.explanation: Safe disposal of faeces prevents germs from reaching water sources.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe sanitation practices that prevent waterborne disease spread.

questions.prompt: Which action is an example of reusing waste?
options: Using an empty yoghurt cup as a seedling pot
Throwing all waste in a river
Leaving broken glass on a path
questions.correctAnswer: Using an empty yoghurt cup as a seedling pot
questions.explanation: Reusing means using an item again for the same or a different useful purpose.
questions.learningOutcome: Give examples of reducing, reusing, and recycling solid waste.

questions.prompt: Why should learners wear gloves when collecting waste?
options: To protect hands from germs and sharp objects
To stop waste from being sorted
questions.correctAnswer: To protect hands from germs and sharp objects
questions.explanation: Gloves reduce contact with dirt, germs, and sharp waste such as broken glass.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety measures when handling solid waste.

questions.prompt: Which source can pollute air in a village or town?
questions.explanation: Smoke carries harmful gases and particles that pollute air.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common sources of air pollution in the local environment.

questions.prompt: Which change of state forms water droplets on the outside of a cold bottle?
questions.explanation: Water vapour in air cools on the cold bottle and changes into liquid droplets.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain condensation using familiar observations.

questions.prompt: Which word processing command stores a document for later use?
questions.explanation: Saving keeps a document in the device storage so it can be opened later.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the save command to store a word document.

questions.prompt: A learner wants a heading to stand out without changing the words. Which formatting tool should be used?
questions.explanation: Bold formatting makes text stand out while keeping the same words.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose appropriate formatting tools for simple word documents.

questions.prompt: Food and drinks should be kept away from computers.
questions.explanation: Spilled food or drinks can damage devices and create electrical hazards.
questions.learningOutcome: Observe safety rules when using computing devices.

questions.prompt: Name one feature used to change the appearance of text in a word processor.
questions.explanation: Text appearance can be changed using features such as font size, font type, colour, bold, italic, or underline.
questions.learningOutcome: Name common text formatting features in word processing.

questions.prompt: A plant has no flowers but has small spores on the underside of its leaves. Which plant is it most likely to be?
questions.explanation: Ferns are non-flowering plants that reproduce using spores.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify plants from observed reproductive features.

questions.prompt: A learner groups maize, hibiscus, and bean together. Which reason best supports the grouping?
questions.explanation: Maize, hibiscus, and bean are flowering plants, so they can be grouped together.
questions.learningOutcome: Give reasons for grouping plants using common features.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why fungi are important in a compost heap?
options: They help break down dead plant materials
They make plastic waste vanish instantly
questions.correctAnswer: They help break down dead plant materials
questions.explanation: Many fungi decompose dead matter and return useful nutrients to the soil.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of fungi in decomposition and soil improvement.

questions.prompt: A learner touches mouldy bread during an investigation. What should the learner do next?
options: Wash hands with soap and water
Eat the bread to test it
Keep the bread in a school bag
questions.correctAnswer: Wash hands with soap and water
questions.explanation: Hands should be washed after handling mould because some fungi may be harmful.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety procedures after observing fungi.

questions.prompt: Which vertebrate group includes animals that start life in water and can live on land as adults?
questions.explanation: Many amphibians, such as frogs, begin life in water and later live on land and in water.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify vertebrates using life processes and habitats.

questions.prompt: Which pair shows a vertebrate and the correct body covering?
questions.explanation: Most fish have scales, while birds have feathers and many mammals have hair or fur.
questions.learningOutcome: Match vertebrate groups to their body coverings.

questions.prompt: Why is a bat classified as a mammal rather than a bird?
options: It feeds its young on milk
questions.correctAnswer: It feeds its young on milk
questions.explanation: Mammals feed their young on milk, even when some, like bats, can fly.
questions.learningOutcome: Use defining features to classify vertebrates correctly.

questions.prompt: A learner has dust in the eye after sweeping. Which first action is safest?
options: Rinse the eye with clean water
Use a sharp stick to remove it
questions.correctAnswer: Rinse the eye with clean water
questions.explanation: Clean water can gently remove dust; rubbing or using sharp objects can injure the eye.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe first steps when caring for sense organs.

questions.prompt: Which activity can help keep bones and muscles strong?
questions.explanation: Exercise strengthens muscles and helps keep bones healthy.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose habits that support healthy bones and muscles.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the work of joints?
options: They allow bones to move where they meet
They digest food in the stomach
They make red blood cells only
questions.correctAnswer: They allow bones to move where they meet
questions.explanation: Joints are places where bones meet and allow bending or other movement.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the function of joints in movement.

questions.prompt: During breathing out, what mainly leaves the lungs?
questions.explanation: Breathing out removes air that contains more carbon dioxide from the body.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe what happens during breathing in and breathing out.

questions.prompt: Which habit best supports a healthy breathing system?
options: Avoiding smoke and dusty places when possible
Breathing smoke to make lungs strong
Closing windows in a smoky room
questions.correctAnswer: Avoiding smoke and dusty places when possible
questions.explanation: Smoke and dust can irritate the breathing system and make breathing difficult.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose practices that protect the breathing system.

questions.prompt: Which observation is a common sign that someone may have a tapeworm infection?
questions.explanation: Tapeworm infection can cause stomach discomfort, weakness, or weight loss and needs health care advice.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize signs and symptoms linked to common internal parasites.

questions.prompt: Which food safety practice helps prevent tapeworm infection?
options: Keeping meat uncovered on the floor
questions.explanation: Proper cooking kills many parasites that may be present in unsafe meat.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify food safety practices that prevent parasite infections.

questions.prompt: A child often walks barefoot near dirty soil. Which parasite risk is increased?
questions.explanation: Jiggers can enter the skin, especially on feet exposed to dusty or dirty ground.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate risky behaviours to external parasite infestation.

questions.prompt: Which combination best prevents the spread of cholera at school?
options: Safe water, handwashing, and clean latrines
Shared cups, dirty toilets, and open water
Raw food, unwashed hands, and uncovered bins
Skipping meals and drinking river water
questions.correctAnswer: Safe water, handwashing, and clean latrines
questions.explanation: Cholera prevention depends on clean water, hygiene, and proper sanitation.
questions.learningOutcome: Combine hygiene and sanitation actions to prevent waterborne diseases.

questions.prompt: Which symptom should make a learner seek help from a trusted adult or health worker after drinking unsafe water?
questions.explanation: Severe diarrhoea can be a sign of a waterborne disease and needs quick attention.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify warning signs of waterborne diseases that require help.

questions.prompt: Which waste management action should come first when trying to reduce school waste?
options: Mix sharp waste with food scraps
questions.explanation: Reducing waste at the source is better than dealing with large amounts of waste later.
questions.learningOutcome: Prioritize waste reduction before reuse and recycling.

questions.prompt: Which waste item should be handled with extra care because it can cut the skin?
questions.explanation: Broken glass has sharp edges that can injure people handling waste.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify risky waste materials and safe handling methods.

questions.prompt: Which action shows recycling?
options: Turning used paper into new paper products
Dropping litter in a drainage channel
questions.correctAnswer: Turning used paper into new paper products
questions.explanation: Recycling changes waste material into a useful new product.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish recycling from reducing and reusing waste.

questions.prompt: Which situation is most likely to increase air pollution around a school?
questions.explanation: Burning rubbish releases smoke and harmful particles into the air.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze human activities that increase air pollution.

questions.prompt: Water is left in an open basin on a sunny day and the level goes down. What change mainly happened?
questions.explanation: Heat from the sun changes some liquid water into water vapour, lowering the water level.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain evaporation using observations from daily life.

questions.prompt: Which process changes liquid water into ice in a freezer?
questions.explanation: Freezing happens when a liquid loses heat and changes into a solid.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate cooling to freezing in common materials.

questions.prompt: Name one way learners can reduce air pollution during a school clean-up.
questions.explanation: Avoiding open burning reduces smoke and harmful particles in the air.
questions.learningOutcome: Suggest practical ways to reduce air pollution in the community.

questions.prompt: A learner typed a paragraph but the title is too small. Which tool should be used?
questions.explanation: Font size changes how large or small the selected text appears.
questions.learningOutcome: Use font size to improve readability in a word document.

questions.prompt: Which sequence is best for creating and keeping a new word document?
options: Open word processor, type text, save document
Switch off device, type text, save document
Pour water, type text, close eyes
Delete file, type text, unplug device
questions.correctAnswer: Open word processor, type text, save document
questions.explanation: A document is created by opening a word processor, entering content, and saving it for later use.
questions.learningOutcome: Follow basic steps to create and save a word document.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to open a document saved yesterday. Which action should be taken?
options: Retrieve or open the saved file
Create a new folder and ignore the file
questions.correctAnswer: Retrieve or open the saved file
questions.explanation: Retrieving a document means opening a file that was saved earlier.
questions.learningOutcome: Retrieve a saved word document from device storage.

questions.prompt: Which action shows safe use of a shared school computer?
options: Pulling cables while the device is on
questions.explanation: Logging out protects personal work and keeps the shared computer ready for the next user.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety and responsibility rules when using shared computing devices.

questions.prompt: Which formatting change is best for showing a book title in a sentence?
questions.explanation: Italic text is often used to make titles or selected words stand out.
questions.learningOutcome: Select appropriate text formatting for a clear document.

questions.prompt: Changing font colour can help highlight important words in a document.
questions.explanation: Font colour can make selected words more noticeable when used carefully.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain uses of font colour in word processing.

questions.prompt: A plant grows from a seed inside a fruit, while another produces spores under leaves. Which conclusion is best?
options: The first is flowering and the second is non-flowering
The first is non-flowering and the second is flowering
questions.correctAnswer: The first is flowering and the second is non-flowering
questions.explanation: Seeds inside fruits show a flowering plant, while spores under leaves suggest a non-flowering plant such as a fern.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare evidence used to classify flowering and non-flowering plants.

questions.prompt: Which investigation would best compare flowering and non-flowering plants safely?
options: Observe leaves, flowers, cones, or spores without tasting any plant
Eat unknown leaves to test the plant group
Burn the plants to see the smoke colour
Pull up every plant in the compound
questions.correctAnswer: Observe leaves, flowers, cones, or spores without tasting any plant
questions.explanation: Observation is enough for classification and avoids unsafe handling or damage to the environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan safe observations for classifying plants.

questions.prompt: A learner says all fungi are harmful. Which evidence best corrects the learner?
options: Unknown fungi should not be eaten
questions.explanation: Some fungi are useful, such as yeast in baking, although others may be harmful.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate claims about useful and harmful effects of fungi.

questions.prompt: Four animals are listed: frog, lizard, goat, and tilapia. Which feature separates the goat from the other three?
options: It feeds its young on milk
questions.correctAnswer: It feeds its young on milk
questions.explanation: All four are vertebrates, but a goat is a mammal that feeds its young on milk.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare vertebrate groups using distinguishing characteristics.

questions.prompt: A learner classifies a crocodile as an amphibian because it swims. What is the best correction?
options: It is a reptile because it has dry scales and lays eggs
It is a bird because it has wings
It is a fish because it has gills
It is a mammal because it has fur
questions.correctAnswer: It is a reptile because it has dry scales and lays eggs
questions.explanation: Swimming alone does not make an animal an amphibian; crocodiles are reptiles.
questions.learningOutcome: Use multiple features instead of habitat alone to classify vertebrates.

questions.prompt: Which plan best protects both ears and learning during a music practice?
options: Keep volume moderate and take breaks
Stand next to very loud speakers for hours
Insert sharp objects to clean ears
questions.correctAnswer: Keep volume moderate and take breaks
questions.explanation: Moderate sound levels and breaks reduce the risk of ear damage.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose protective habits for ears in noisy environments.

questions.prompt: A learner bends the elbow to lift a book. What explains the movement best?
options: Muscles pull bones at a joint
The skin pushes air into bones
The skull controls the elbow directly
questions.correctAnswer: Muscles pull bones at a joint
questions.explanation: Movement happens when muscles contract and pull bones around a joint.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how muscles, bones, and joints work together in movement.

questions.prompt: Why does breathing become faster after running?
options: The body needs more oxygen and must remove more carbon dioxide
The stomach stops all body work
questions.correctAnswer: The body needs more oxygen and must remove more carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: During exercise, body cells use more oxygen and produce more carbon dioxide.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate exercise to changes in breathing rate.

questions.prompt: Which school poster message best combines parasite prevention and dignity?
options: Wear shoes, keep floors clean, and seek help for itchy feet
Share dirty combs to save time
questions.correctAnswer: Wear shoes, keep floors clean, and seek help for itchy feet
questions.explanation: Prevention should be practical and respectful, with care for anyone affected.
questions.learningOutcome: Promote respectful prevention and management of external parasites.

questions.prompt: A family stores boiled water in an open bucket and dips cups into it. What is the main risk?
options: The water can become contaminated again
The water turns into a solid immediately
questions.correctAnswer: The water can become contaminated again
questions.explanation: Safe water can be contaminated again if stored uncovered or touched with unclean cups.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze safe water storage practices that prevent contamination.

questions.prompt: Which set of actions best manages waste after a class snack break?
options: Sort waste, reuse clean containers, and put the rest in proper bins
Sweep all waste into the school drain
Burn plastic wrappers beside the classroom
Leave peels and wrappers on desks
questions.correctAnswer: Sort waste, reuse clean containers, and put the rest in proper bins
questions.explanation: Sorting and proper disposal make waste management safer and cleaner.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan practical solid waste management in school settings.

questions.prompt: Why is burning plastic waste a poor way to reduce litter?
options: It causes air pollution and can harm health
It changes plastic into clean drinking water
It makes soil more fertile immediately
It safely removes all harmful gases
questions.correctAnswer: It causes air pollution and can harm health
questions.explanation: Burning plastic releases smoke and harmful gases, so safer waste methods should be used.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate waste disposal methods based on environmental health.

questions.prompt: Which observation shows both evaporation and condensation in one activity?
options: Steam rises from hot water and forms droplets on a cool lid
Ice stays solid in a freezer
A stone remains dry in sunlight
Paper is folded into a plane
questions.correctAnswer: Steam rises from hot water and forms droplets on a cool lid
questions.explanation: Water changes to vapour by evaporation and then back to liquid droplets by condensation.
questions.learningOutcome: Connect multiple changes of state in a simple investigation.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to test whether heat affects evaporation. Which fair test is best?
options: Place equal water amounts in sunny and shaded places and compare levels
Use different amounts of water in many containers
Add soil to one cup and oil to another
Measure one cup today and another next month
questions.correctAnswer: Place equal water amounts in sunny and shaded places and compare levels
questions.explanation: A fair test changes one factor, heat from sunlight, while keeping the water amount the same.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a simple fair test about evaporation.

questions.prompt: Which choice best improves a typed class notice before printing?
options: Use a clear title, readable font size, and save the file
Use tiny text and never save
Use many random colours for every word
questions.correctAnswer: Use a clear title, readable font size, and save the file
questions.explanation: A useful notice is readable, organized, and saved before printing or sharing.
questions.learningOutcome: Create clear and readable word documents for communication.

questions.prompt: A document was saved with the name ScienceNotes. What should a learner check first when trying to retrieve it?
options: The folder or location where it was saved
The number of desks in class
questions.correctAnswer: The folder or location where it was saved
questions.explanation: Knowing the saved location helps a learner find and open the correct file.
questions.learningOutcome: Use file names and storage locations to retrieve saved documents.

questions.prompt: Which action best protects a word document from being lost during editing?
questions.explanation: Saving regularly keeps recent work stored if the device closes unexpectedly.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe document-saving habits during word processing.

questions.prompt: Which safety rule protects both learners and computing devices in a lab?
options: Keep cables tidy and walk carefully
Run between desks with wet hands
questions.correctAnswer: Keep cables tidy and walk carefully
questions.explanation: Tidy cables reduce tripping risks and help protect devices from being pulled down.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze safe physical arrangements in a computer lab.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why learners should use meaningful file names?
options: They make saved documents easier to find later
They stop the keyboard from working
They change all text to pictures
questions.correctAnswer: They make saved documents easier to find later
questions.explanation: A meaningful file name helps users identify and retrieve the right document.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of meaningful file names.

questions.prompt: Suggest one safe rule for learners sharing a computer in class.
questions.explanation: Safe sharing includes respecting other users' work, logging out, and keeping passwords private.
questions.learningOutcome: Suggest rules for responsible use of shared computing devices.

questions.prompt: A school garden has maize, bean, fern, and moss. Which table heading would best separate the plants for a Grade 5 science display?
options: Flowering plants: maize and bean; non-flowering plants: fern and moss
Fungi: maize and bean; animals: fern and moss
Water plants: all four plants; desert plants: none
Poisonous plants: all four plants; useful plants: none
questions.correctAnswer: Flowering plants: maize and bean; non-flowering plants: fern and moss
questions.explanation: Maize and bean are flowering plants, while fern and moss do not produce flowers.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a classification display using common local plant examples.

questions.prompt: Which class activity best teaches both usefulness and safety of fungi?
options: Observe yeast in dough and discuss why unknown fungi should not be eaten
Taste every mushroom found near school
Keep mouldy bread in desks for many weeks
Throw fungi samples at other learners
questions.correctAnswer: Observe yeast in dough and discuss why unknown fungi should not be eaten
questions.explanation: This activity shows a useful fungus while reinforcing safe handling and eating rules.
questions.subStrandTitle: Economic Importance and Safety of Fungi
questions.learningOutcome: Plan a safe learning activity about useful and harmful fungi.

questions.prompt: A learner sorts animals by habitat only and puts crocodile and fish in the same group. Which question would best improve the classification?
options: What body covering and breathing structures does each animal have?
Which animal is drawn first in the book?
Which animal has a shorter name?
questions.correctAnswer: What body covering and breathing structures does each animal have?
questions.explanation: Using features such as body covering and breathing structures gives a better vertebrate classification than habitat alone.
questions.learningOutcome: Refine animal classification by asking questions about key features.

questions.prompt: A dusty classroom makes several learners cough. Which combined response is most scientific and safe?
options: Open windows, reduce dust by cleaning safely, and move coughing learners away from dust
Close all windows and sweep faster without masks
Burn rubbish indoors to hide the dust smell
Tell learners to hold their breath all lesson
questions.correctAnswer: Open windows, reduce dust by cleaning safely, and move coughing learners away from dust
questions.explanation: Ventilation, safe cleaning, and reducing exposure protect the breathing system.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a safe response to environmental conditions affecting breathing.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best links the skeleton, muscles, and safety in games?
options: Bones support the body, muscles move bones, and safe play prevents injuries
Muscles protect all computers from viruses
Bones digest food faster during games
Joints stop all movement during exercise
questions.correctAnswer: Bones support the body, muscles move bones, and safe play prevents injuries
questions.explanation: Understanding how the body moves helps learners choose safe ways to play and exercise.
questions.learningOutcome: Connect body structure, movement, and injury prevention during physical activity.

questions.prompt: A community wants to reduce waterborne disease after heavy rain. Which plan is strongest?
options: Protect water sources, treat drinking water, wash hands, and use clean latrines
Drink flood water because it is fresh
Store water in open containers beside animals
Stop washing hands to save soap
questions.correctAnswer: Protect water sources, treat drinking water, wash hands, and use clean latrines
questions.explanation: Waterborne disease prevention works best when safe water, hygiene, and sanitation are combined.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a community-level plan to reduce waterborne disease risk.

questions.prompt: A learner has repeated stomach pain and may have worms. Which action is most responsible?
options: Tell a parent or teacher and visit a health worker
Buy unknown medicine from another learner
Ignore the pain for many months
questions.correctAnswer: Tell a parent or teacher and visit a health worker
questions.explanation: A trusted adult and health worker can guide safe testing, treatment, and prevention.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose responsible actions for suspected parasite infection.

questions.prompt: Which school waste project best shows reduce, reuse, and recycle working together?
options: Use fewer disposable items, make planters from clean containers, and collect paper for recycling
Burn all waste and buy more disposable cups
Mix food waste with broken glass and leave it outside
Throw plastic bottles into a river after class
questions.correctAnswer: Use fewer disposable items, make planters from clean containers, and collect paper for recycling
questions.explanation: The project reduces waste, reuses containers, and sends paper for recycling.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a waste management project using reduce, reuse, and recycle principles.

questions.prompt: A group wants to prove that evaporation can be reversed by condensation. Which setup is best?
options: Heat water gently and hold a cool lid above the vapour to collect droplets
Freeze a dry stone and weigh it
Mix soil and sand in a dry cup
Fold paper and unfold it again
questions.correctAnswer: Heat water gently and hold a cool lid above the vapour to collect droplets
questions.explanation: Heating produces water vapour, and a cool lid changes the vapour back into liquid droplets.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan a simple investigation showing evaporation and condensation.

questions.prompt: A learner is preparing a one-page science report on waterborne diseases. Which word processing plan is best?
options: Type clear headings, use readable formatting, save with a meaningful file name, and log out after printing
Use random symbols, avoid saving, and leave the account open
Type without spaces and delete the title
Share the password so others can change the report
questions.correctAnswer: Type clear headings, use readable formatting, save with a meaningful file name, and log out after printing
questions.explanation: A good document is clear, saved properly, and handled safely on shared devices.
questions.learningOutcome: Create and manage a clear word document while following device safety rules.
